topic: The Impossible Chessboard: Decoding Information Theory

sections.title: The Hook: The Warden's Challenge
lecture_lines: Warden places 64 coins on a chessboard grid.
One coin is flipped to hide the secret square.
Prisoner must identify the square to win freedom.
animations: Display a 8x8 grid of coins with mixed Heads (#FFD700) and Tails (#C0C0C0).
Highlight one square as the 'Warden's Choice' with a flashing white (#FFFFFF) square outline.
Show a prisoner and Bender appearing on screen.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Binary Encoding
lecture_lines: 64 squares are represented by 6 binary bits.
Bit positions 0 through 63 define every square.
XOR parity acts as our digital checksum.
animations: Display binary index '000000' through '111111' on top of the 64 squares.
Visualize the XOR sum of indices as a 6-bit string changing color to #FF5733 when updated.
Animate individual binary digits flipping from 0 to 1 with a pulse effect.

sections.title: The Information Strategy
lecture_lines: Target square index is encoded into board parity.
Calculate XOR sum of all Heads positions.
Flip the one coin to match target index.
This ensures board parity equals target square.
Information is hidden within coin state distribution.
animations: Display the current XOR sum of all Heads as a 6-bit number.
Highlight the target index chosen by the warden.
Show the XOR sum transforming to match the target index after one coin flip.

sections.title: Mathematical Proof via Parity
lecture_lines: Flipping one coin changes exactly one parity bit.
This effectively corrects the total parity sum.
Parity acts as an error detection mechanism.
Mathematically map board state to unique square.
Proof confirmed: always identify the secret square.
animations: Render a diagram of the parity XOR sum logic.
Flash the coin being flipped in #00FF00 to show the parity shift.
Show the parity sum updating to the target index in real-time.

sections.title: Conclusion: Information Theory Significance
lecture_lines: Strategy applies Error Correction Code principles.
Information theory minimizes uncertainty via parity.
Technology uses this to fix data corruption.
animations: Display a QR code graphic representing data structure.
Pulse a parity bit within the structure in #00FFFF.
Final summary text fading in with a bright white (#FFFFFF) background glow.
